whatThisIsFor: A returned verdict outranks an active-owner claim. A lane that has returned is not still verifying, and a family its verifier failed is not awaiting a verdict.
obligationVocabularyNote: The P2V rows record thirteen obligations as strings and two as booleans. Both are read; a third spelling refuses, because reading only the strings turned two passing obligations into failures and doubled the defect count.
supersessionRule: one current verdict per family, ordered by the base each row DECLARES it read at: a read whose verifiedAtBase descends from another read's base is the later one and supersedes it. Where neither base is an ancestor of the other, a row that declares a commit-shaped base outranks one that declares none. Lane precedence (factory vf lanes over codex-cloud directories, then higher lane number) decides only when neither row says when it read. An exact owner-confirmed substantive selection in LEGAL_HOLD_RECLASSIFICATION_2026-09-04.json preserves environment-scoped BLOCKED_SOURCE history without letting that environment refusal remain a legal hold; it expires on the next substantive read at or after the record's Captain SHA. Recency is never inferred from file modification or merge time. Superseded rows remain as history with superseded: true

failedObligations.finding: A MANDATORY SWORN SELECTION IS UNMADE AND UNDISCLOSED, AND THE GUIDE DIRECTS ITS TWO CONDITIONAL SUB-BLANKS UNCONDITIONALLY. Full detail in exactDefect.

evidence.component: primary_filing (CR-65, Petition for Expungement of Records, Rev. 10/2024)
evidence.page: CR-65 page 6 (PDF page 6 of 11) — canonical and boundary, both families
evidence.field: CR-65:Check Box2.0 and CR-65:Check Box2.1 — the two boxes of the sworn item '(3) (Select one of the following)': 'that I have not previously applied for an expungement in this or any other jurisdiction' / 'that I have previously filed for an expungement'
whatIsWrong: NEITHER BOX IS MARKED in the delivered bytes. Read at 150 dpi on all four fixtures (both families, canonical and boundary). This is a mandatory selection on a page headed 'I swear or affirm, under the penalty of perjury', so the packet is delivered with a required attestation unmade.

THE GUIDE NEVER TELLS THE PARTICIPANT TO MAKE IT. participant-instructions.md contains no occurrence of 'Select one', 'previously applied', 'previously filed' or 'pro se' in either family (case-insensitive grep, zero hits).

WORSE, THE GUIDE DIRECTS THE TWO DEPENDENT BLANKS UNCONDITIONALLY. Its 'Required before filing' section opens 'Fill every item below on both the canonical and boundary-style packet before filing' and then lists, as items 20 and 21, 'County where any previous expungement was filed' and 'Court case number of any previous expungement'. Those two blanks exist only on the SECOND branch of the unmade selection. A participant who has never sought an expungement and follows the instruction literally writes a county and a case number for a prior expungement that does not exist, on a page sworn under penalty of perjury, while the attestation that governs those two blanks stays empty.

The 'pro se (Not represented by an attorney)' box on the same page is also unmarked and also undisclosed, on a packet whose entire attorney block is refused as 'attorney-only; no representation fact is held'.
evidence.whyTheCountersCannotSeeIt: production-field-map.json classifies both boxes as refusals with reason 'A genuine participant election not determined by this route', refusalClass 'participant_sworn_narrative_or_legal_election', isSelectionControl true, routeDetermined false, and NO requiredBeforeFiling flag. completeness-contract.mjs makes PARTICIPANT_ELECTION_GENUINE an allowed disposition that — unlike REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING — carries no DISCLOSED condition, so writeGuides() never surfaces it and requiredOptionsMissing reads 0. The counter accepts the field map as its classification authority, which is the same blind spot FIX09 recorded.
evidence.positiveControlThatThisZeroIsReal: Marks DO render on these fixtures and this lane proved it twice on the same bytes before believing any absence: (1) C-10-CRIMINAL page 1 (PDF page 9) shows a visible tick in the 'STATE OF ALABAMA' caption box (field Check Box1.0) at 150 dpi; (2) al-felony-dwop-set CR-65 page 3 (PDF page 3) shows a visible tick against the dismissed-without-prejudice Section III ground (field Check Box10.3). A probe that read only text extraction would have been enough here, but the rasters were read as well because the withdrawn-finding precedent in this cohort was a probe that missed marks drawn as stroked paths.
evidence.corroborationThatThisIsAGapAndNotHouseSt: ar-nonconviction-seal-set, an official_pdf_fill sibling in the same factory, ships the exactly analogous control — ACIC petition paragraph 2's four situation boxes, all four unmarked — and its guide says in terms: 'The petition's own paragraph 2 states the four situations this packet covers, and you must tick exactly one.' Alabama ships the same shape of control with no such sentence.
evidence.exactRepair: Surface the item (3) selection and the pro se box to the participant. Either declare them requiredBeforeFiling with printed captions so writeGuides() lists them, or add an explicit sentence in the shape Arkansas already uses. AND make the two dependent blanks conditional in the guide: 'only if you tick the second box in item (3)'. The unconditional 'Fill every item below' over a conditional item is the harmful half.

failedObligations.finding: Seven declared writes are directions masquerading as known facts. Three charge fields print 'The charge shown on the certified case record'; two grounds fields print 'See the selected statutory route and attached certified records'; and two arresting-agency fields print 'Agency shown on the certified arrest record'. These strings are visibly written into the official form, while the instructions do not tell the participant to replace them with facts. The mechanical counter remains zero and therefore misses this defect.

The production map records 63 required refusals, but 33 labels copied into participant-instructions.md literally contain 'undefined' (from 'Complete undefined' through numbered variants). That does not meaningfully name the fields. The instructions also fail to state the registry's required signature, notarization, filing-fee, and waiver actions as clear participant steps.

The committed registry has four stops. The packet covers prosecutor or victim objection, contested hearing, disposition/fact mismatch, and immigration consequences, but it omits the same registry condition's licensing and firearm consequences.

failedObligations.evidence: The instructions state flatly: 'There is no filing fee for this petition,' sourced three ways from the compiled Arkansas profile's Act 1460 lines. But the petition this packet delivers prints, at paragraph 9: 'The Defendant has paid all filing fees required to be paid with the filing of this Petition mandated by A.C.A §16-90-1419.' The proposed order prints the same sentence at paragraph 10. Grepping participant-instructions.md for '16-90-1419', '1419' and 'paragraph 10' returns nothing. So a participant is handed a sworn petition containing a paragraph asserting they have paid fees under a named statute, while the instructions tell them no fee exists and never mention that the paragraph is there. The instructions' fallback — 'If the clerk … nevertheless asks you to pay something, that is a question about that court's own practice' — treats the possibility as a clerk's practice question when the trap is printed on the packet's own face. A4's recorded practice is that the near-miss is named and disposed of, as the sibling ms-misd-addl-set packet does for Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 in this same lane. Here it is not named at all.

Two of four are carried and two are absent. Carried: [0] the prosecuting attorney objects and [1] the court sets a contested hearing, both in one bullet quoting the registry's own handoff line. ABSENT: [2] 'Immigration, licensing or firearm consequences are in play.' A case-insensitive grep of participant-instructions.md for immigra, firearm, licens and citizen returns exactly one hit — the phrase 'a lawyer licensed in Arkansas' — and the same grep over the extracted text of both petition fixtures and both order fixtures returns nothing at all. ABSENT: [3] 'Whether the participant falls in the covered historical population is unclear.' The registry's own destination detail explains what that means — 'A narrow historical population. Opening the route is gated on current eligibility-source review.' The nearest bullet the packet carries is about paragraph 3's target-offence definition under A.C.A. § 16-93-1202(10)(A), which is a different question: whether the offence qualifies, not whether this participant falls inside the Act 531 historical cohort at all. Neither the phrase 'historical population' nor any equivalent appears. Every one of the other seven families in this lane carries an immigration or citizenship stop condition; this is the only packet of the eight with none.

failedObligations.finding: The packet asserts a silence the repository does not have. Its "The filing fee" section reads the petition's paragraph 3 correctly — a sworn statement that fees "mandated by A.C.A § 16-90-1419" have been paid — and correctly reports that no amount is printed on the form, which this lane confirmed by extracting the source PDF's text (paragraph 3 names the fee statute and no figure appears anywhere on the face). But it then tells the participant that "no source this packet holds establishes it" and sends them to ask the clerk what the § 16-90-1419 fee is. The repository establishes it. The compiled Arkansas profile — cited as a requiredSourceId for this exact route in the national route census — states it three separate ways: packetGenerator.feeRules[1] "Sealing petition filing fee $0 — Filing fees eliminated by the 2019 amendments", feeRules[0] "Act 1460 eliminated sealing filing fees; the real costs are records and any counsel", and filingDestinationRules[1] "File in the circuit or district court that handled the case. Act 1460 eliminated filing fees for sealing." The profile's sourceFormStatements[7] ties this to the very form in this packet: "Petition and Order to Seal Arrest (Act 1460) — Arrest records under § 16-90-1409." Amendment A1 settles the ordering: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer; if it does, the packet states it, and a named checkable authority may stand in only where no held source establishes it. Here one does, so the stand-in is unavailable and the packet substitutes a question for an answer the repository holds. The consequence is not cosmetic: paragraph 3 is sworn, and a participant told to go and pay an unknown fee before signing is being sent to resolve something the repository says was abolished in 2019. The repair is for a repairer with the legal record in front of them, not for this lane: state what the profile holds and reconcile it with the form's paragraph 3, which still recites the fee statute. Whether the correct sentence is "$0, fees eliminated by the 2019 amendments" or a reconciliation of the two is a drafting and counsel question; asserting repository silence is not an available answer.

failedObligations.finding: The service mechanics are right and the objection clock is wrong in a way that can mislead a felony-class petitioner. Correct: two recipients from the form's own Certificate of Service (the prosecuting or city attorney, and the arresting agency), the form's two methods, and the rule that the certificate is completed only after service. The defect is the objection window. The packet leads with a flat "The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object", sourced to the committed packet-set manifest. I traced that sentence: it is data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/AR.memo.json rules.service, and it appears VERBATIM on 11 of the 12 Arkansas tracks in that file — including ar-felony-seal, where the same repository's compiled profile says the window is 90 days. A line that is provably wrong on a sibling track it is attached to is state-level boilerplate, not a route-addressed determination, and under A3 (holding is per FACT, not per document) it does not establish this route's answer. The record that DOES address it is the compiled profile's own table: "Prosecutor objection window - misdemeanor 30 days / felony 90 days, Receipt / filing of petition". That rule is self-applying here, because the delivered petition prints "A Class _____ [_] felony [_] misdemeanor" and the participant supplies the class. So the repository establishes a determinate class-keyed rule and the packet publishes a flat number from a non-route-held line, demoting the real rule to "the longer window MAY apply to you". It then sends a statutory question to an office that cannot answer it: "ask the clerk of the court where you file which window that court runs" — the window is set by statute, not by court practice, and A1 permits a named authority to stand in only where no held source establishes the fact. The contrast is inside this same builder's own work: ar-misdemeanor-dwi-seal-set resolves the identical conflict correctly by naming its route's class ("this packet is a misdemeanour DWI or BWI conviction, which puts it in the 30-day limb"). The repair is one paragraph: state the class rule as the rule, cite the profile, and drop the clerk sentence. Recorded separately: the three-day service deadline comes only from that same 11-track boilerplate — the compiled profile contains no "three days" and the form prints none — but it errs toward serving early, so I record it as a provenance limit rather than a failure.

(1) The committed route census row for obligation:track-only:AR:ar-nonconviction-seal records destination.detail '§ 16-90-1410(b). Venue for an acquittal and for charges never filed is not stated.' (3) The same entry carries unresolvedQuestions[0] 'Venue for an acquittal and for charges never filed is not stated in § 16-90-1410(b)' with impact BUILD_BLOCKER and affectedElement 'venue', sourced to LegalEase-Arkansas-Legal-Review.md TRACK AR-5. The packet shipped all four and stated one destination for all four. failedObligations.finding: THE ROUTE-LEVEL REFUSAL IS CORRECT; A SOURCED SENTENCE INSIDE IT IS FALSE ABOUT THE RECORD IT NAMES. What is right, and should survive the repair: no committed record this packet binds states a filing fee or a fee waiver for § 61-14-9 — this lane searched the compiled West Virginia profile and the route contract and found no fee keyed to 61-14-9 — and the packet names a specific checkable authority, the office of the clerk of the West Virginia circuit court in the county of conviction or juvenile adjudication, in the same breath as the refusal. That is DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 theStandard.met limb three, and the packet's A3 discipline in refusing to import a sibling section's figure is exactly what A3 was written to protect. WHAT IS WRONG: the delivered canonical and boundary bytes, on the filing-instructions page, print 'The compiled profile carries no-fee lines keyed to W. Va. Code Sec. 61-11-25 and a $200 figure keyed to Sec. 61-11-26; this route is Sec. 61-14-9 and is neither of them.' THE COMPILED PROFILE CONTAINS NO $200. A search of src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WV-west-virginia.json for '$200' returns ZERO hits. What the profile actually records for 61-11-26, in its feeRules and twice more in its fee section, is: 'For 61-11-26 conviction expungement, the circuit clerk charges the same fee as filing a civil action, and a person who receives an expungement order must pay a $100 West Virginia State Police processing fee.' So the sentence is wrong twice over — wrong on the amount ($100, not $200) and wrong on the character of the charge (a civil-action fee plus a $100 processing fee payable on grant, not a flat $200 filing fee). The $200 figure IS held in this repository, but by different records: the route-obligation census and the packet-family build worklist record 'the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee of $200' for the 61-11-26 families. The packet attributes to the compiled profile a figure the compiled profile does not carry. Under A4's operative rule — a false sentence 'fails under whichever obligation carries the false sentence' — this one is carried by the fee paragraph. The repair is one clause, not the paragraph: correct the attribution, or drop the sibling aside entirely, and leave the § 61-14-9 refusal and its named authority exactly as they stand.

If the criminal history record is not submitted along with this form, your submission will be deemed incomplete and your request for a review and/or hearing will be denied.' The packet therefore tells the participant to disregard a documented requirement whose breach the source says causes denial. This finding does NOT depend on mapping the gated form to the track — it needs only that the packet asserted an unqualified negative about what the record contains, and that assertion is false against the repository at this base. The correct treatment is to state that a DESPP form in the library imposes the ≥01/01/2024 record date and that the participant should obtain a current report and confirm with DESPP, rather than to instruct them to ignore it.

THE PARTICIPANT'S OWN NAME IS WRITTEN INTO FOUR WIDGETS THAT CANNOT HOLD IT, AT A FONT SIZE 0.01pt ABOVE THE READABLE FLOOR, AND EACH APPEARANCE STREAM CLIPS IT. This is the boundary fixture, whose job is to find exactly this. METHOD: every flattened widget appearance in fixtures/packet-boundary-filled.pdf was decoded from its Form XObject — the /BBox, the clip path, the /Tf size and the hex Tj string — and the required text width was computed with pdf-lib's Helvetica metrics at that widget's own size and compared with that widget's own usable width. The value is the 70-character boundary name 'Alexandrina-Katharine Montgomery-Vandenberg-Oyelaran y Fitzwilliam III', set at 6.01pt, requiring 195.97pt. Every appearance stream carries an explicit clip, 'W n', inset 1pt on each side. FOUR OF THE SIXTEEN WIDGETS WITH TEXT CANNOT TAKE IT: /FlatWidget-7888911063 on page 1, BBox 196.99, usable 194.99, over by 0.98pt; /FlatWidget-2708199956 on page 7 at x=332.887 y=463.385, BBox 187.88, usable 185.88, OVER BY 10.09pt; /FlatWidget-6703682664 on page 7 at x=406.387 y=449.662, BBox 161.12, usable 159.12, OVER BY 36.84pt; /FlatWidget-9668333493 on page 9 at x=124.733 y=493.345, BBox 182.19, usable 180.19, OVER BY 15.78pt. The same string fits in the ten other widgets it is written into, which range from 200.98 to 342.16. WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT THE PERMITTED REFUSAL: docs/RCAP_OREGON_OFFICIAL_PDF_GRADE_A_LANE_C.md protects a value that is REFUSED at the 6pt readable floor and left blank for the participant. This value was not refused. reports/rendered-artifacts.json lists exactly two unfittable refusals on the boundary fixture — cap-COUNTY and Address, both with reason value_exceeds_widget_width_at_minimum_font — and cap-PetitionerFullName is not among them; it was written. THE LIKELY MECHANISM, offered as a lead and not as a finding: production-field-map.json records ONE writeBox for cap-PetitionerFullName, on page 1, rect width 210.08, rectBasis 'acroform_widget_rect_read_from_the_document'. The AcroForm field has fourteen widget kids across ten pages with widths from 161.12 to 342.16. A fitter that sizes to one recorded rect and applies the result to every kid produces exactly this: a size that fits the box it measured and overruns three others. WHAT THE PARTICIPANT SEES: a PDF viewer honours the Form XObject clip, so the name is truncated mid-word on the filed pages rather than printed over neighbouring text. On page 7 the surname is cut off in the line 'Contemporaneous with the filing of this notice, ______ has filed'; on page 9 in the order's own 'Petitioner, ______,'. The canonical fixture is clean: 26 widget appearances, zero exceeding their clip box. RESIDUAL LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: this is a geometric computation from the appearance streams, not a pixel reading. This lane inspected no raster. The central raster receipt for this family records 0 problems over 30 pages, which is not a contradiction — a clip guarantees no ink lands outside its box, so an ink-outside-the-box check cannot see a value truncated inside one. The two instruments answer different questions and this one answers the question the Lane C rule is about.

There are three. reports/actual-writes.json reports 3 values in each fixture -- petitioner_name, date_of_birth, phone_number -- and I confirmed the absence on the delivered bytes rather than on the report: extracting page 1 of both fixtures with pdftotext -bbox-layout and reading the band that contains the mailing_address write box (field-map rect x=105 y=484 w=171 h=13, which is y_top 295-308 on a 792pt page), the only words present are the form's own printed captions 'Mailing Address:', 'City:', 'State:', 'Zip:' at x=28.42-100.93, 280.42, 415.42 and 514.42. The 171-point run from x=105 to x=276 is empty in the canonical fixture and empty in the boundary fixture. This is the A4 defect with its sign reversed -- the rule is that a packet may never tell a participant it does not state something it does state, and the harm here is the mirror image and worse in direction: a participant who reads the component table and believes the address is on the form will not transcribe it, and will file a petition with the Probation Service that has no address on it to answer. The packet contradicts itself three times over in the participant's favour -- 'Your address is not filled in, and that is deliberate', the street-address row in the items-to-supply table, and 'The whole address - street, city, state and zip' in the deliberately-left-blank list -- which is exactly why a reader cannot tell which sentence to believe. failedObligations.finding: ONE OF THE FIVE STOP CONDITIONS THE REGISTRY HOLDS FOR THIS TRACK IS ABSENT FROM THE PACKET IN ANY FORM, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COSTS A PARTICIPANT THE ROUTE. I compared data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json trackId ma-expunge-time selfHelpStopConditions against participant-instructions.md and the delivered bytes, condition by condition, then grepped each condition's distinguishing terms. (1) 'Any offence may fall on the Sec. 100J list, several entries of which turn on facts rather than charge titles' -- carried: the packet reproduces the whole exclusion list. (2) 'Whether every offence occurred before the 21st birthday is unclear' -- carried, first bullet in both the md and the delivered page. (4) 'The district attorney objects' -- carried. (5) 'The court sets a hearing on the best interests of justice' -- carried in substance; the guidance states the hearing rule and 'the determination that expungement is in the interests of justice'. (3) 'WHETHER OFFENCES AROSE FROM A SINGLE INCIDENT FOR COUNTING PURPOSES IS UNCLEAR' -- ABSENT. The words 'incident', 'arising from', 'arose', 'counting' and 'count as one' appear NOWHERE in participant-instructions.md and NOWHERE in the delivered canonical bytes; I grepped each. What the packet does say is 'your record shows more than two convictions, or more than two non-conviction records - the section limits it to two.' The same registry entry holds the rule that resolves it, in its exclusions: 'More than two records. MULTIPLE OFFENCES ARISING FROM THE SAME INCIDENT COUNT AS ONE.' So the repository establishes both the counting rule and that uncertainty about it is where self-help stops, and the packet publishes neither. The direction of the harm is specific and one-way: a participant with three charges from one arrest reads the two-record limit, counts three, and abandons a route they are eligible for -- and no bullet tells them this is the moment to ask. Under A2 a committed registry is a held source; under A4 as extended, an obligation whose failure mode is omitting a fact the repository establishes is an ask-the-repository-first obligation. Both limbs are met and the omission is the whole of the failure.

Both recompute from disk: NV.memo.json 113a9728...(312293) and legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json 6076f734...(3683419). THE DEFECT IS THE SECOND ONE. The receipt's bindingMethod — rewritten by this very repair — now reads 'each bound by exact SHA-256 over its committed bytes AT BUILD TIME'. The family was built at d6b594038 on 2026-09-01, where that record stood at 80d88d69...(3674510); it was still 713ed7ab...(3677644) at the later pagination fix a120d8bd5 on 2026-09-04; the pinned digest 6076f734... first exists at d798dc66b on 2026-09-04, AFTER both. So the sentence is false: nothing bound those bytes at build time because those bytes did not exist. And unlike its three siblings in this same cohort and same repair window, the receipt carries NEITHER an identityRefresh block (AR, OK, WA all have one) NOR an exactObject canonical digest (NC has two). A reader cannot tell from this receipt that the record moved at all. failedObligations.finding: The repair added a well-drafted section that names a checkable authority, and it still fails, because it asserts a silence the repository does not have. The section states: "No held source establishes what it costs to file a CPL 160.59 sealing application", that neither application source states a filing fee, states that filing is free, or describes a fee waiver, and that the packet "does not supply a figure it does not hold" — then names the clerk's office of the court of conviction and sentencing as the office to ask. The claim about the two forms is correct and this lane confirmed it independently: extracting the text of both the application and the pro se packet from the mounted corpus finds no fee, cost or dollar figure anywhere on either face. But the claim about the repository is false. The compiled New York profile, cited as a requiredSourceId for this exact route, answers it directly: packetGenerator.feeRules[2] reads "CPL 160.59 sealing application — No separate filing fee — Court motion; notarization needed", and the profile's narrative repeats it — "the 160.59 motion itself carries no separate filing fee" — and its agent guidance says to note that the motion has no separate filing fee. Amendment A1 settles the ordering: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer, and a named checkable authority may stand in only where none does. One does here, so the stand-in is unavailable and the packet sends the participant to ask a question the repository already answers. The packet's third paragraph shows it can do this correctly — it states the certificate-of-disposition fee, $5 outside New York City and $10 in the five boroughs, sourced to the form's own face, and the compiled profile's feeRules[0] and [1] hold exactly those figures. The repair is to state the no-separate-filing-fee answer the profile holds alongside the certificate fee it already states, and to carry across the waiver-adjacent facts the profile also holds — that legal-aid organisations and county district attorney sealing units assist pro se applicants at no cost.

No confirmed statewide schedule exists.' apply_fee_waiver -- 'In forma pauperis relief is available; the Court of Common Pleas Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis is published statewide', with conditionDescription 'Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.' THE DELIVERED SENTENCE, participant-instructions.md line 89, quoted whole: 'The filing fee and whether it can be waived, who must be served and by what method, and the addresses the petition is served on are not established in this repository. Ask the same clerk. An unsourced figure in a filing instruction would be worse than none.' And line 105: 'The fee-waiver motion (PA-IFP-CCP) is held as exact source evidence only. It is not generated into your packet and nothing on it is a blank on this filing. If you need a fee waiver, ask the clerk for the current form.' SIDE BY SIDE: the record says in forma pauperis relief IS available and the statewide motion IS published; the packet says whether the fee can be waived is 'not established in this repository' and sends the participant to the clerk for 'the current form' -- while this repository holds that exact statewide form, bound by exact SHA-256 in this family's own source-receipt.json at b1255ef0...(760989 bytes) and resolved by content hash in this container. The record's caution about the AMOUNT ('no confirmed statewide schedule exists', 'roughly $132 to $215') is a reason to name no figure, which the packet's last sentence defends well; it is not a reason to tell a participant that the availability of a waiver is unknown when the controlling record says it is available. WHETHER THE RECORD IS OPEN: it is not. The wave-2 return at 677700997 blocked this obligation as MISSING_ARTIFACT_SPECIFIC_APPROVAL_INPUT on the finding 'County filing fees vary, no confirmed statewide schedule exists, and conditional use of the IFP motion requires participant/local confirmation. The exact fee/waiver branch cannot be resolved from the controlling record.' On the record as it now stands that premise does not hold: the branch is resolved and its condition is the participant's own election, stated in the manifest as 'Applies only where the participant seeks to proceed in forma pauperis.' A branch conditioned on a participant's choice is a settled treatment, not an open legal question.

failedObligations.finding: The canonical petition receives nine writes; the boundary petition receives seven. The two that vanish are the petitioner's own state and ZIP. scripts/build-census-v1-pa_pardon_expungement-set.mjs holds them for the boundary persona — participant.state "Pennsylvania" and participant.zip "18702-2214" (lines 271-272) — and maps both as WRITE to the AddrState and AddrZip widgets (lines 108-109). Neither reaches the bytes: pdftotext over fixtures/boundary--PA-RCRIM-P-790-PETITION.pdf and over the assembled boundary.pdf finds no 18702 and no 18702-2214, and the delivered address block reads "Address: 1188 Upper Notch Crossing Road, Apartment 14B" on one line and "Wilkes-Barre Township" on the next, with no state and no ZIP. The cause is a width refusal and the refusals are substantively correct: I measured the widgets from the field map and the strings with pdf-lib's Helvetica metrics, and at the 6 pt readable floor "Pennsylvania" is 35.23 pt against an 18.21 pt widget and "18702-2214" is 32.02 pt against a 31.85 pt widget — 0.17 pt too wide. Under docs/RCAP_OREGON_OFFICIAL_PDF_GRADE_A_LANE_C.md refusing at the floor is correct behaviour; what makes this a failure is the second half of that rule, that the blank is left FOR THE PARTICIPANT. Nothing records either refusal: reports/actual-writes.json carries no refusal entry for the boundary petition, reports/builder-completeness-counters.json reports invisibleWrites 0, and neither AddrState nor AddrZip appears among the field map's 78 requiredBeforeFiling entries or anywhere in participant-instructions.md. On the long-value persona the packet therefore delivers a court filing whose petitioner address has no state and no ZIP, and never tells the participant to write them in.

The 78 declared required-before-filing blanks are disclosed properly and I checked every one of the 78 labels against participant-instructions.md myself: zero missing, and each names the page, the field, the printed context, why the platform holds no value and what the participant must supply. The failure is what is not on the list. The two widget-refused values above are blanks the participant must now fill and they are not among the 78, not on the page, and not classified anywhere. The list is complete against the builder's own declaration and incomplete against the delivered artifact — which is exactly the gap the Oregon rule exists to close.

Every one of the six delivered PDFs rehashes byte-exact to its recorded sha256 and byteLength, and pdf-lib page counts agree with every record: assembled canonical and boundary 5 pages each, petition 1, order 2. On hashes and counts there is nothing wrong. What fails here is the completeness of the artifact record: the boundary artifact carries two fewer writes than the canonical artifact of the same document and no record in the family explains the difference. reports/actual-writes.json lists 7 boundary petition writes against 9 canonical with no refusedWrites, no unfittable list and no note; reports/builder-completeness-counters.json reports invisibleWrites 0 and findings empty. A reader of the artifact record cannot tell that two values were refused, and a reader of the artifact cannot tell that two values are missing.

Two things fail together and the second is the serious one. First, structurally: the packet has no "when to stop and get help" section at all, on either the guidance page or in participant-instructions.md, and none of the registry's three selfHelpStopConditions is carried as a stop. The participant has not yet obtained a pardon, which the registry says is out of scope and a referral, is nowhere. Whether the pardon is conditional or unconditional cannot be determined from the document is reduced to a description of the difference between the two. The record still appears after the quarterly cycle and the fallback route's availability is unclear is not carried as a stop. Second, and this is a DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A4 violation on the delivered bytes: the guidance page, packet pages 4-5 of both fixtures, tells the participant "This page states no timetable and no criterion for that, because neither is established by the two forms this packet is built from, and an unsourced criterion in a filing instruction is worse than none." The timetable IS established, for this exact route, in three committed records I read at this base. The track registry's packetInstructions for pa_pardon_expungement says "Tell the participant a pardon does not by itself erase the record, and that the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly." Its manualCompletionItems carry "Quarterly verification date — Guidance, verification schedule — The participant records when they checked whether the automatic route cleared the record", listed as required before filing. Its packetSet condition on the petition component reads "Generated only where the automatic route has not cleared the record after the quarterly cycle." And src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/PA-pennsylvania.json states "the Board of Pardons transmits eligible records to AOPC quarterly, AOPC sends the record to the court of common pleas, and the court orders expungement after confirming the criteria." The same packet states the quarterly cycle on another page — participant-instructions.md paragraph 4 says the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly, in bold. So the packet tells the participant, on the page that goes in the envelope, that it does not state something it states on the page that does not. The guidance page compounds it by narrowing its own source universe to "the two forms this packet is built from", which is precisely the narrowing A2 forbids: the repository's committed records are held sources, not just the PDFs. The registry's named verification schedule is absent from the guidance page in consequence.

I only went looking because two earlier lanes had failed this obligation on this cohort (vf29/vf37 on Oklahoma, vf02 on Nevada) and a verifier does not get to overturn a finding it did not re-measure. The probe: for every page of every fixture, take the first non-blank line and flag it when it continues a contact block opened on the previous page (PRINTED NAME / MAILING ADDRESS / TELEPHONE / EMAIL) or is a bare postcode fragment following a MAILING ADDRESS; separately count non-whitespace characters per page and read every thin page rather than trusting a threshold. My first threshold of 200 characters would have MISSED the boundary fixture's split page at 216 characters, which is why every flagged page was then read, and the two decisive pages were also rendered at 150 dpi and looked at.

failedObligations.finding: Four declared required-before-filing blanks contradict facts printed by the platform on the same forms. On both route primary filings the packet prints the participant's full name and date of birth, then leaves C1 applicant name and C2 date of birth blank and says for all four that the platform holds no value. participant-instructions.md likewise says the platform filled the name and date of birth, then lists those same C1/C2 items as facts the participant must supply. In both fixtures this duplication is visible in the PDF bytes (canonical Jordan Avery Reyes / 1991-04-17; boundary Maria-Alejandra O'Shaughnessy-Whitfield / 1968-12-31). The vacation pleading also misstates the existing sentencing-case cause number as a case number the court may assign at filing: the motion caption says 'if the court assigns one at filing', the proposed order says 'if one was assigned', and the instructions repeat that treatment, although the committed track asks the participant for the cause number and the records checklist directs them to the existing sentencing-court docket.

All three component byte ranges exist, but the required component semantics do not. The registry marks wi_exp_certificate_of_discharge_followup-status-request-2 conditional and says it is used only when the participant wants to know whether the certificate issued rather than ask that it be issued. Both production-field-map.json and reports/rendered-artifacts.json record componentConditions as an empty object. The participant component table omits the only-if condition, while its generic steps direct the participant to fill every page for the route and file the pages together. The packet therefore directs both mutually distinct requests to every participant instead of preserving the registry's status-only condition.

Primary-request page 1 visibly leaves a TO/addressee line and tells the participant to write that office's name and address there. The registry independently requires the current mailing address of the supervising authority before sending. That blank is absent from production-field-map.json, blanks-left-for-the-participant.json and the primary request's required-items table, so it is unclassified and undisclosed. At the same time, the field map classifies a nonexistent primary-filing-1.case_number as protected even though the repaired primary letter explicitly says it is not filed with a court and no court assigns it a case number. The participant instructions compound the error by saying every case number in every caption is left blank until the court assigns one at filing, even though the real status-request page has a participant-supplied existing case or docket number.

The request pages themselves name the correct administrative destination: send to the supervising or detaining authority, with the resulting certificate going to the clerk of circuit court. But participant-instructions.md affirmatively contradicts those pages by calling the act a filing, directing the participant to file the pages for the route, and saying the court assigns a case number at filing and all pages are filed together. The registry says in terms: not a court filing; send the written request to the supervising or detaining authority. Participant-facing instructions cannot contradict that destination.

(1) The certificate refusal is not merely narrow on this route; it is false, and false in the expensive direction. The packet carries the same paragraph as its conviction sibling, word for word: "The certificates themselves cost more than the application, and this packet does not state that amount because BCI sets it per applicant." The canonical fixture this family ships prints "$65.00" three times on packet pages 17 and 18, on the BCI Application for Certificate of Eligibility the packet itself delivers. Confirmed in this lane with pdftotext against this family's own committed bytes (SHA-256 8efb78f3f885af303bc74f461172d319f63b60bb747720329e401c1bd4d417f4), not taken from any brief or report. DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A4 states the rule in one line: a packet may never tell a participant that it does not state something it does state. A SECOND and independent limb fails here, and it is the A1/A2/A3 one rather than A4's internal-consistency rule. The compiled Utah state profile (src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/UT-utah.json, SHA-256 73dd7ea988d0673dca3b8bf657f2df090d062c0821f8c0662a57ccfac8e7660d) states: "eligible conviction, plea-in-abeyance, or special certificates may require an additional $65 per case; no certificate issuance fee is required for dismissals, acquittals, or declinations." This route is a dismissal without prejudice. Applying A3's per-fact, per-route test rather than reading the document as a whole: the exempting limb names "dismissals" without qualification, and the limb that does carry a charge names conviction, plea-in-abeyance and special certificates, none of which is this route. A dismissal without prejudice is a dismissal and is not a plea in abeyance, so the exemption reaches it. The repository therefore establishes that the certificate issuance fee for this route is nil, and A2 lists the compiled state profile for the family's jurisdiction as a held source in its own right. The packet nonetheless tells the participant that it cannot state the amount and sends them to ask BCI — which is precisely what A1 forbids where the record already answers. The residual ambiguity is stated rather than resolved: the profile's word is "dismissals", unqualified, and a lane wanting certainty should read the BCI FAQ the profile cites before publishing $0. What passes on this obligation is not in dispute and is recorded so the repair does not disturb it: the court filing fee of $150 is stated and sourced to the row the packet fills on 1044XX page 2, and the court waiver route is named as Utah form 1305GE under Utah Code 78A-2-302 and CJA Rule 4-508.

THE RECORD, in three places and in terms: legal-design-track-registry.json track ut_pet_limitations rules.service reads 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. failedObligations.finding: The packet tells the participant that it does not state an amount that its own delivered pages print. participant-instructions.md carries, in bold: "The BCI certificate carries a separate fee, and this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant." The canonical fixture this family ships prints "$65.00" three times on packet pages 17 and 18, on the BCI Application for Certificate of Eligibility the packet itself delivers. Confirmed in this lane with pdftotext against this family's own committed bytes (SHA-256 ad594f0a40750195b67e36916f3628df5b96d337e4955c9063b415747d6e36d6), not taken from any brief or report. DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A4 states the rule in one line: a packet may never tell a participant that it does not state something it does state. The A1/A2 limb does NOT add a second failure here, and saying so is part of the finding. failedObligations.finding: The verdict is unchanged from the prior lane's, but the reason recorded there no longer describes this packet, and the difference matters for the repair. The determination's notReExamined entry says this family carries "no amount, no no-fee statement and no office to ask". That was true when the determination was written at 2026-09-02T00:45:00Z. Ninety-four seconds later, commit 077f685 (FIX04) added a "What this costs" section that does name an office to ask — the Crime Information Bureau of the Wisconsin Department of Justice, Criminal History Unit, pointing to the mailing address the form prints in instruction 1 — so the true-silence finding is spent. Re-measured honestly against the standard as it now stands, this still fails, on the other limb. The packet says "no source held in this repository states a fee for a fingerprint record removal request, states that there is none, or describes a waiver." That statement is false. The compiled Wisconsin profile, cited as a requiredSourceId for this exact route, answers the question directly in four places: packetGenerator.feeRules[1] "DOJ-CIB fingerprint arrest removal — Wisconsin DOJ says no fee is required", with feeRules[2] drawing the distinction that matters, "DOJ-CIB criminal background check — Fee-based through WORCS"; and pathways[0].ruleClauses[24], pathways[1].ruleClauses[5] and sourceSections[4] each state that Wisconsin DOJ says the request uses DJ-LE-250B, requires fingerprints, and has no fee. The route census repeats it in this family's own destination detail: "There is no fee for the removal request; the background check that precedes it is fee-based." Amendment A1 settles the ordering — ask first whether the repository establishes the answer, and a named authority may stand in only where none does. One does here, so the stand-in is unavailable. The packet is right that the form's two pages are silent, and this lane confirmed that independently; it is wrong that the repository is. The repair is to state the no-fee answer the profile holds and to carry across the distinction the profile draws between the free removal request and the fee-based WORCS background check that precedes it.
